### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the always-executed activities A15, A17 and A18 sat around two-thirds through the case (mean relative position about 0.64), while the intermittently executed A14, A16 and A19 sat around one-third through (about 0.34–0.35) in the roughly three in ten traces that contained them. In the later window the picture is reversed: A15, A17 and A18 now sit around one-third through (about 0.38) and A14, A16 and A19 around two-thirds through (about 0.67–0.68). [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006]
- The order between the two groups reversed in all 21 tested activity pairs. Six pairs that co-occur in every trace flipped completely: A15, A17 and A18 each followed A20 and A24 in all 200 earlier traces and now precede them in all 200 later traces. Pairs involving the intermittent activities flipped in the traces where both occur (for example, A14 preceded A15 in about 60 of 200 earlier traces and follows it in about 65 of 200 later traces). Co-occurrence shares stayed essentially the same, and the intermittent activities never appeared without the mandatory ones in either window. [REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021]
- A20 and A24, executed in every trace, moved modestly later: A20 from about 0.38 to about 0.44 and A24 from about 0.57 to about 0.64 of the trace length. [POS007, POS008]
- Distances between consecutive activities changed: A25 now follows A24 at a distance of two steps instead of four, and A20 now follows A35 at a distance of four steps instead of two, in essentially all traces of both windows. [LAG001, LAG002]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports the possibility that two groups of activities exchanged their place in the sequence: the intermittently executed A14, A16 and A19, which previously ran in the first third of the case ahead of the always-executed A15, A17 and A18, now run in the final third after them, with A20 and A24 still lying between the groups but slightly later than before; the A35-to-A20 distance growing from two to four steps fits A20's later position. The reversal is shown directly by the relational items, is complete in all 200 traces for the six pairs between A15/A17/A18 and A20/A24, and the positional shifts point the same way; participation rates barely moved, so this is a reordering of activities that already existed rather than activities being added, removed or made optional. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL008, REL015, REL020, LAG002]

Chance is an unlikely account of this pattern: screening produced 31 qualifying control-flow items where about 0.32 would be expected in an unchanged process — roughly one hundred times the chance expectation — and every item's difference is larger than those seen in about 995 of 1000 random re-splits of the two windows. [POS001, POS002, POS003, POS004, POS005, POS006, POS007, POS008, REL001, REL002, REL003, REL004, REL005, REL006, REL007, REL008, REL009, REL010, REL011, REL012, REL013, REL014, REL015, REL016, REL017, REL018, REL019, REL020, REL021, LAG001, LAG002]

Limitations: the position and lag indicators use event positions rather than clock time, so on their own they would not establish that an activity was moved — here the relational items show the order change directly, but the evidence says nothing about timing in clock terms. The order within each group (for example A14 versus A16, or A15 versus A17) was not tested, so the evidence cannot show whether the three intermittent activities moved as one block or separately. An important competing explanation is a change in repetition or looping around these activities, which can also displace positions; against it, no tested pair shows interleaved or repeated execution in either window. [REL001, REL008, REL015, LAG001]

Other differences: the share of traces containing the intermittent activities drifted slightly (A14 about 60 vs 65 of 200 traces, A16 about 69 vs 58, A19 about 71 vs 77), a difference a finite sample can produce even without a change; and the A24-to-A25 spacing tightened from four steps to two, a change around A24/A25 that the group exchange does not by itself explain. [POS001, POS003, POS006, LAG001]
